newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker as correction continues.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker as correction continues.

text.p: Toronto stocks extended the recent correction in equity markets on Thursday as investors turned their attention to key U.S. jobs data on Friday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 22.58 points to close at 5826.56 in turnover of 94.14 million shares worth C$1.59 billion ($1.14 billion).
Declining stocks outpaced advances 573 to 366 with 299 issues unchanged.
"This is a market that has been waiting to correct for ages and it's very orderly," said Dunnery Best, director of private client investing for Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell nearly 40 points as U.S. investors braced for the release of key jobs data on Friday.
Economists said on Thursday that strong numbers may prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again as a pre-emptive strike against inflation.
Another U.S. rate hike would heap pressure on the Bank of Canada to raise domestic rates to defend the local currency.
The Canadian dollar finished sharply weaker on Thursday after earlier hitting its lowest level since April 4, 1995 as offshore investors pressed for a rise in Canadian rates, traders said.
Of the Toronto Stock Exchange's 14 sub-groups, 10 ended softer led by base metals, energy and consumer products. The strong side included communications and media.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. gained 0.23 to 3.43 on turnover of 5.02 million before trading in the volatile stock was halted. It was the third time this week that heavy trading in Bre-X has overwhelmed the TSE's outdated trading system.
The stock was unhampered on the Nasdaq, Montreal and Alberta exchanges.
* Sherritt International Corp. instalment receipts fell 0.25 to 54.75 on volume of 7.14 million shares.
